drills.title: Follow the Pass
drills.subtitle: Pass, follow your pass to that spot. Catch it at cone 3, drive and shoot.
drills.blurb: Full ice, two-sided. Lines along each goal line; the front player at the boards passes first. Catch at cone 3, drive, shoot, and join the other line.
drills.diagramAlt: Full-ice diagram of Follow the Pass. Lines sit on both goal lines, three cones mark each side, and the flow ends with a shot before joining the far line.
coachingPoints: Full ice and two-sided. Both ends run at the same time.
The front player starts at the boards and makes the first pass.
Three cones per side: near blue line at centre, boards at the red line, far blue line at centre.
Catch the puck at cone 3, drive the net, and shoot. Then join the line at the other end.
steps: Set a line along each goal line. The first player in each line starts on the boards with a puck.
Place three cones on each side of the rink: centre ice at the near blue line, on the boards at the red line, and centre ice at the far blue line.
The front player passes to the next player in line, then follows that pass along the cones.
Each player who receives the puck passes it on and follows their own pass. Keep the puck and the skaters moving up the ice.
The player who catches the puck at cone 3 (far blue line, centre) drives the net and shoots.
After the shot, that player joins the line at the far end. The same pattern is already coming back the other way.

drills.title: Low-to-High: D Shot
drills.subtitle: Carry in, drive to the dot, curl, pass up to the D. D shoots.
drills.blurb: Half-ice zone entry. Carry in, drive to the dot, curl toward the boards, and pass up to the D. The D shoots and the forward drives the net.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Low-to-High D Shot. The forward curls at the dot, passes up the wall to the defence, the defence shoots, and the forward drives the net.
coachingPoints: Half-ice zone entry with one defence inside the blue line.
Carry in with speed, drive to the faceoff dot, then curl toward the boards.
The pass is low-to-high: from the curl, up the wall, onto the defence.
Defence shoots. The forward drives the net front, then returns to the line.
steps: Forwards line up just outside the blue line with pucks. One defence stands inside the blue line, on the boards side of the entry.
Carry the puck over the blue line and drive toward the faceoff dot.
At the dot, curl toward the boards so you are looking back up the wall.
Pass low-to-high, up the boards, to the defence.
The defence catches and shoots. Drive to the front of the net for a tip or a rebound.
Leave the net and return to the back of the line. The next forward goes.

drills.title: Low-to-High: Give-and-Go
drills.subtitle: Carry in, drive to the dot, curl, pass up to the D. Give-and-go.
drills.blurb: Same zone entry. After the low-to-high pass, the D gives it back to the forward cutting the slot, and the forward shoots.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of the low-to-high give-and-go. The forward passes up to the defence, cuts to the slot, takes the return pass, and shoots.
coachingPoints: Use the same entry as D Shot: carry, dot, curl, pass up the wall.
The forward leaves as the pass goes. The cut to the slot starts with the pass.
Defence returns the puck. One touch back if it is there.
The forward shoots from the slot, then returns to the line.
steps: Set it up like Low-to-High: D Shot. Forwards outside the blue line, one defence inside on the strong-side wall.
Carry in, drive to the faceoff dot, and curl toward the boards.
Pass low-to-high to the defence.
As soon as the pass leaves your stick, cut to the slot.
Defence passes the puck back to the forward on that cut.
The forward shoots, then returns to the back of the line.

drills.title: Low-to-High: D-to-D
drills.subtitle: Carry in, drive to the dot, curl, pass up to the D. D-to-D, shot.
drills.blurb: Same zone entry. The bottom D passes across to the top D, the top D shoots, and the forward screens.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of low-to-high D-to-D. The forward passes to the bottom defence, the puck goes across to the top defence for a shot, and the forward screens.
coachingPoints: Same forward entry, with two defence on the ice.
Bottom D is on the strong-side wall and moves the puck. Top D is across the blue line and shoots.
The D-to-D pass stays up near the blue line, firm and flat.
The forward screens the goalie, stick on the ice, then clears the front.
steps: Forwards line up outside the blue line with pucks. Bottom defence stands inside the blue line on the boards side of the entry. Top defence stands on the far side of the blue line.
Carry in, drive to the faceoff dot, and curl toward the boards.
Pass low-to-high to the bottom defence.
Bottom defence passes across the blue line to the top defence.
Top defence shoots. The forward drives the net and screens the goalie.
Clear the front of the net and return to the back of the line.

drills.title: 1 Up / 1 Down
drills.subtitle: Gap and angling 1v1. D touches the goal line, F touches the blue line, then play it out.
drills.blurb: Corner 1v1. On 'Go' the D touches the goal line and the F touches the blue line. The coach puts the puck in, the F attacks for a shot and a rebound, and the D gaps up and angles.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of 1 Up / 1 Down. The defence skates to the goal line, the forward skates to the blue line, the coach passes to the forward, the forward attacks and shoots while the defence closes the gap and angles.
coachingPoints: Use all four corners. Corners that share a net take turns.
D: head up before you turn up ice, close the gap, and lead with your stick to steer the forward to the outside.
F: look before you turn to attack, use speed and fakes, and protect the puck on the way to the net.
F gets one shot and one rebound. If the D steals it, clear it or skate it past the top of the circles.
steps: Set a forward line and a defence line in the corner. The coach stands near the top of the circle with pucks.
On the coach's 'Go', the D skates down and touches the goal line while the F skates up and touches the blue line.
The coach puts the puck in to the forward.
The forward attacks the net. The D steps up, closes the gap, and angles the forward to the outside.
The forward gets one shot and one rebound. If the D wins the puck, they clear it or skate it past the top of the circles.
Flip roles: the forward joins the D line and the D joins the F line. Halfway through, swap corners for new matchups.

drills.title: Olympic Breakout to 2-on-1
drills.subtitle: 3-on-0 breakout to the blue line, tight turn around the cone, then back in 2-on-1 against the same D.
drills.blurb: A half-ice drill with three players: one D, a winger and a centre. The D gets the coach's rim and passes to the winger on the wall, who hits the centre curling low, and the forwards carry it up to the blue line while the D gaps up. The centre makes a tight turn around the cone on the blue line, the winger turns too, and they come back in on a 2-on-1 against the same D. Waiting lines stand in the neutral zone.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of the Olympic Breakout to 2-on-1. Waiting D, centre and winger lines stand in the neutral zone outside the blue line. A coach at the top of the zone rims the puck behind the net. The D starts in front of the net, gets the puck beside it and passes to the winger on the half-wall. The centre swings low and curls up the middle for a pass from the winger while the D skates up to the top of the circles. The centre carries the puck to a cone on the blue line and loops tightly around it, and the winger turns on the wall side. They come back in 2-on-1 as the D skates backward; the centre passes to the winger, who shoots on the goalie.
coachingPoints: D: shoulder-check on the way to the puck, then a hard, flat pass to the winger's forehand.
Winger: back to the boards at the hash marks, stick on the ice.
Centre: swing low and curl up the middle with speed, ready for the pass.
Centre: go all the way around the cone, tight to it, puck on the inside, head up coming out.
D: gap up, then pivot and skate backward. Stay in the middle and take away the pass.
Forwards: one pass to beat the D, then shoot.
steps: Setup: one D in front of the net and a cone on the blue line. Waiting lines stand in the neutral zone outside the blue line: D high, centres in the middle, wingers on the bottom boards. The coach has the pucks. Only the D, one winger and one centre go each time.
The coach rims the puck behind the net. The D goes to get it and the winger skates down to the half-wall at the hash marks.
The D passes to the winger on the wall while the centre swings low through the slot.
The winger passes to the centre curling up the middle. The D gaps up toward the top of the circles.
The centre carries the puck and the winger skates up to the blue line.
Tight turn at the blue line: the centre loops around the cone with the puck and the winger turns on the wall side. The D pivots and skates backward.
2-on-1: the centre passes to the winger to beat the D, and the winger shoots.
Everyone goes back to their line in the neutral zone and the next D steps in front of the net.

drills.title: Zone Exits: Bounce Pass
drills.subtitle: Bounce a self-pass off the boards around a cone, then a soft D, then a stretch pass past the D.
drills.blurb: Defensive-zone exits from a line in each corner. Start with a self-pass off the boards around a cone, swap the cone for a coach as a soft D, then finish with a bounce stretch pass to a teammate past the D holding the line.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of the zone-exit bounce pass progression. In the bottom corner a player carries up the wall, banks the puck past a cone, and exits. In the top corner a player carries up the wall and banks a stretch pass past the coach at the point to a teammate at the blue line.
coachingPoints: Progression 1: bank the puck off the boards past a cone, skate around it, and pick it up.
Progression 2: replace the cone with a coach as a soft D. Same self-pass, now with pressure.
Progression 3: bounce a stretch pass off the boards to a teammate for the exit.
Pick the angle and weight so the D holding the blue line can't pick the pass off.
steps: Set a line in each corner on the goal line with pucks. Place a cone low on one wall. A coach stands at the point on the other side.
The first player carries up the wall toward the cone.
Bank the puck off the boards past the cone, skate around the inside of the cone, pick it up, and exit over the blue line.
Progression 2: the coach replaces the cone as a soft defender. Bounce it past them the same way.
Progression 3: the player in the other corner carries up the wall while a teammate swings to the boards at the blue line.
Bank a stretch pass off the boards past the D to the teammate, who carries it out.
Players switch lines and the next pair goes.

drills.title: Tip-and-Dig Shooting
drills.subtitle: Tip the point shot into the empty net, dig it out, and shoot on the goalie.
drills.blurb: Zone shooting with two nets: an empty net at the hash marks and the regular net with a goalie. Tip the point shot into the empty net, dig it out, and shoot on the goalie.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Tip-and-Dig Shooting. A shooter at the blue line shoots through a tipper standing in front of an empty net at the hash marks. The tipper digs the puck out and carries into the slot to shoot on the goalie.
coachingPoints: Put an empty net at the hash marks. The goalie stays in the regular net on the goal line.
Tipper: stick on the ice and redirect the point shot into the empty net.
Dig the puck out of the net quickly, then attack the slot and shoot on the goalie.
Run it in both corners at the same time if you have the ice.
steps: Place an empty net at the hash marks. One player stands in front of it as the tipper. The shooters line up at the blue line with pucks.
The first shooter shoots from the blue line and the tipper deflects it into the empty net.
The tipper digs the puck out of the empty net while the shooter moves in to become the next tipper.
The tipper carries into the slot and shoots on the goalie.
After the shot, go to the back of the shooting line. The next shooter goes.

drills.title: 4-Lane Warm-up
drills.subtitle: One line in the corner. Lane 1 inside edges, lane 2 crossovers, lanes 3 and 4 carry the puck and shoot.
drills.blurb: Full-ice warm-up. Cones split the ice into four lanes and one line starts in the corner. Skate lane 1 on inside edges, lane 2 with crossovers, then carry a puck two-handed in lane 3 and one-handed in lane 4, with a shot at the end of each.
drills.diagramAlt: Full-ice diagram of the 4-Lane Warm-up. Three rows of cones split the ice into four lanes. A skater goes down lane 1, back up lane 2, carries a puck down lane 3 to shoot on the far net, and carries back up lane 4 to shoot on the near net.
coachingPoints: Three rows of cones split the ice into four lanes. One line starts in the corner.
Lane 1: inside edges, no crossovers. Lane 2: outside edges with crossovers.
Lane 3: two hands on the stick, carry and shoot. Lane 4: one-handed carry, then shoot.
Send the next player when the one ahead reaches the first cones.
steps: Set three rows of cones the length of the ice to make four lanes. The line starts in the corner. Put pucks at each end.
Lane 1: skate down the ice on inside edges with no crossovers.
Lane 2: come back up the next lane using outside edges and crossovers.
Lane 3: pick up a puck, carry it two-handed down the lane, and shoot on the far net.
Lane 4: pick up a puck, carry it one-handed back up the last lane, and shoot on the near net.
Return to the line in the corner and repeat.

drills.title: Crossover Circles Race
drills.subtitle: Race around your circle with crossovers, then race to the one puck. Winner attacks, loser plays D. 1-on-1, shoot.
drills.blurb: A skating race on the two end-zone faceoff circles. Each line stands on a neutral-zone faceoff dot near the blue line, and there is ONE puck in the middle of the ice, halfway between the blue line and the tops of the circles. One skater from each line races into the zone and around their circle with crossovers, then exits the circle and races to the puck. The first one there attacks; the loser plays D. 1-on-1 to the net and shoot. For the pivot version, see Crossover Circles: Pivot Race.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of the Crossover Circles Race. A line stands on each neutral-zone faceoff dot near the blue line, and one puck lies in the middle of the ice halfway between the blue line and the tops of the circles. One skater from each line skates into the zone and all the way around the outside of their end-zone faceoff circle with crossovers. Both exit the circle and race to the puck. The winner picks it up and attacks the net; the other racer skates in and defends, skating backwards (dotted arrow). The attacker shoots on the goalie.
coachingPoints: Knees bent and chest up. Push with the outside leg and cross the inside leg over.
Lean into the circle and keep your stick on the ice.
Exit the circle at full speed and race to the puck.
Win the race? Protect the puck and attack the net.
Lose the race? You're the D. Get between the attacker and the net.
Switch directions every round so both crossovers get work.
steps: Split into two lines, one standing on each neutral-zone faceoff dot near the blue line. The coach puts ONE puck in the middle of the ice, halfway between the blue line and the tops of the circles.
Race! The front skater on each line skates into the zone and all the way around their faceoff circle with crossovers.
Exit the circle and race to the puck.
The first one there picks it up and attacks. The other racer plays D.
1-on-1 to the net. Shoot!
Both racers go to the back of their line. The coach puts a new puck down. Next round, go the other way.
Variation (step 2): see Crossover Circles: Pivot Race. One lap around the circle with a pivot at every cone, then race to one loose puck.

drills.title: Crossover Circles: Pivot Race
drills.subtitle: Race: one lap around the circle, pivot at every cone. Then race to the puck. First one there shoots.
drills.blurb: The step-2 version of the Crossover Circles Race. Lines stand on the neutral-zone faceoff dots near the blue line, with one puck in the middle of the ice. Each racer skates into the zone and does ONE lap around the circle with a pivot at each of the 3 cones: forwards, backwards, forwards, backwards. Then turn forwards and race to the puck. First one there picks it up and shoots.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Crossover Circles: Pivot Race. A line stands on each neutral-zone faceoff dot near the blue line, three numbered pivot cones sit on each end-zone circle, and one puck lies in the middle of the ice, halfway between the tops of the circles and the blue line. The racer skates into the zone and does one lap: forwards to cone 1 and pivot to backwards, backwards to cone 2 and pivot to forwards, forwards to cone 3 and pivot to backwards, backwards to finish the lap. Then both racers turn forwards and race to the puck. The first one there picks it up, skates in and shoots on the goalie; the other racer arrives just behind. Forwards skating is a solid arrow, backwards skating is a dotted arrow.
coachingPoints: One lap, pivot at every cone. First to the puck shoots.
Pivot: open your hips toward the middle of the circle, keep your feet moving, eyes up.
Backwards: stay low with your shoulders square, push with crossunders.
After the last pivot, turn forwards fast and sprint to the puck.
Get there second? Keep skating and backcheck the shooter.
steps: Same setup as the Crossover Circles Race: a line on each neutral-zone faceoff dot near the blue line. Put 3 cones on each circle, spread evenly. The coach puts ONE puck in the middle of the ice, halfway between the tops of the circles and the blue line.
Race! Skate into the zone and go forwards to cone 1. Pivot to backwards.
Backwards to cone 2. Pivot to forwards.
Forwards to cone 3. Pivot to backwards.
Backwards to finish the lap, then turn forwards and race to the puck.
First one to the puck picks it up and shoots.
Both racers go to the back of their line. The coach drops a new puck and the next pair goes.

drills.title: Stops and Starts
drills.subtitle: Goal line to far blue, stop, back to near blue, stop, then to the far dots. No pucks first, then with pucks.
drills.blurb: Waves of skaters start on the goal line, sprint to the far blue line, stop hard, sprint back to the near blue line, stop, then finish at the far end-zone dots. The far net stays free for the goalies.
drills.diagramAlt: Full-ice diagram of Stops and Starts. Three skaters on the left goal line sprint to the far blue line, skate back to the near blue line, then sprint to the far faceoff dots, with a goalie in the right net.
coachingPoints: Hard two-foot stops: knees bent, weight on the edges, shoulders level.
Explode out of each stop with short, quick first strides.
Stop facing the same way each time, then switch sides on the next rep.
With pucks: keep the puck close through the stop and the restart.
steps: Skaters start in waves on the goal line.
Sprint to the far blue line and stop hard.
Sprint back to the near blue line and stop hard.
Sprint to the far faceoff dots and stop. Leave the net end free for the goalies.
Run it without pucks first, then the same with pucks.

drills.title: Edges: Cone Weave
drills.subtitle: Weave through a lane of cones from the blue line to the goal line on your edges. Theme: balance and edge work.
drills.blurb: Three or four lanes of cones run from the blue line to the goal line. Skaters weave through their lane on deep edges, then return up the outside to their line.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Edges: Cone Weave. Four lines start at the blue line and weave through lanes of five cones toward the goal line, then skate back up the outside.
coachingPoints: Long strides on one foot: glide and hold the edge round each cone.
Knees bent and weight over the skate you are on.
Inside and outside edges both: carve, don't step round the cone.
Head up, eyes on the next cone.
steps: Set up 3 or 4 lanes of cones from the blue line to the goal line.
The front of each line weaves through the cones on deep edges.
At the goal line, skate back up the outside to your line.
The next skater goes as soon as the one ahead passes the second cone.

drills.title: Lateral Step-overs with Pivots
drills.subtitle: Sideways crossover step-overs down a lane of cones, pivoting 180 degrees at each cone.
drills.blurb: Skaters move sideways down a lane with crossover step-overs, pivoting at each cone so they face the benches, then away from the benches, then the benches again.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Lateral Step-overs with Pivots. Three lines move sideways from the blue line toward the goal line, stepping over to each of three cones and pivoting at each one.
coachingPoints: Stay low and step the trailing leg over the lead leg.
Shoulders and hips stay square to the way you are facing.
Quick, tight pivots at each cone: don't drift past it.
Keep your stick on the ice in front of you.
steps: Set up lanes of cones from the blue line to the goal line.
Step over sideways to the first cone, facing the benches.
Pivot and step over to the second cone, facing away from the benches.
Pivot and step over to the third cone, facing the benches again.
Skate back up the outside to your line.

drills.title: Cone Relay with Pucks
drills.subtitle: Relay race: at each cone, one pass and catch with your line. Alternate forwards (tight turn) and backwards (pivot).
drills.blurb: Three or four lines race at once, each with 3 or 4 cones. At each cone the skater makes one pass to the next player in line and gets it back, alternating forwards with tight turns and backwards with pivots.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Cone Relay with Pucks. The middle lane is drawn: the skater carries forwards to cone 1 with a tight turn, passes to the line and gets it back, skates backwards to cone 2, then forwards to cone 3, and races back to hand off.
coachingPoints: Tight turns: get low, lean in, and keep the puck on the inside.
Pivot without stopping your feet.
Firm, flat passes. Show a target with your stick for the return.
Race, but stay in control: a missed pass costs more time than a slower turn.
steps: Set up 3 or 4 lines with 3 or 4 cones in each lane.
Carry the puck forwards to cone 1 and make a tight turn.
Pass to the next player in your line and get it back, pivot, and skate backwards to cone 2.
Pass and catch again, then go forwards to cone 3 with a tight turn.
Pass and catch, race back, and hand the puck to the next player. First line done wins.

drills.title: 2v2 Point Shot Small Area Game
drills.subtitle: 2 on 2 in a corner with a point player. Dump in, battle, use the point for shots, regroup on a turnover.
drills.blurb: Groups of five at each corner net: 2 O, 2 D and a point player. The point dumps the puck in and the 2v2 starts. The team with the puck can use the point for shots. On a change of possession, regroup up to the point.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of 2v2 Point Shot. The point player dumps the puck into the corner, an O player wins it and carries up the wall, passes to the point, and the point shoots on the corner net while the other O goes to the net.
coachingPoints: Win the race to the puck and protect it along the wall.
Use the point: move it up, then get to the net for tips and rebounds.
On a turnover, regroup to the point before you attack.
D: stick on puck, body on body, and clear the front of the net.
steps: Put a net in each corner. Groups of 5 per net: 2 O, 2 D and 1 point player (or a coach at the point with groups of 4).
The point dumps the puck into the corner and the 2v2 starts.
The team with the puck can pass up to the point for a shot.
On a change of possession, move the puck up to the point before attacking.
Goal or 60 seconds: O and D swap. Each group gets 1 turn on O, 1 on D and 1 rest.

drills.title: 2v2 Hard Rim
drills.subtitle: Rim it hard around the boards to your partner, then 2 on 2. D must touch the top of the circle first.
drills.blurb: Two lines of forwards with pucks at the hash marks and two D at the dots. The first forward rims the puck hard behind the net to the partner on the far wall, and it's 2 on 2. The D must touch the top of the circle before they can defend.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of 2v2 Hard Rim. The top forward rims the puck around the boards behind the net to the bottom forward while the two D skate to the top of the circles. The bottom forward collects, passes to the partner, and the partner shoots.
coachingPoints: Rim it hard and high on the glass side so it gets all the way around.
Receiver: get to the wall early, stop the puck with your skate or stick, and look up.
D: touch the top of the circle, then attack fast and take away the middle.
Play it out: second chances and rebounds count.
steps: Two lines of forwards with pucks at the hash marks on each wall. Two D start at the dots.
The first forward rims the puck hard behind the net to the forward at the front of the other line.
The D must skate up and touch the top of the circle before they can play.
The forwards play 2 on 2 to the net.
If the D win the puck, they pass or rim it to the next pair in line. Then the D go out and the O become D.
Start from the blue line for longer rims. Run the same drill on the other side of the ice.

drills.title: 3v3 Circle Game
drills.subtitle: 3 on 3 at a faceoff circle with two nets. Only one player per team inside the circle.
drills.blurb: Two nets face each other inside a faceoff circle. It's 3 on 3, but only one player per team can be inside the circle. Outside players try to work a pass into their inside player, and they can shoot too.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of 3v3 Circle Game. Two nets with goalies face each other across a faceoff circle. The coach passes to an outside X player, the X players move it around the outside, pass to the inside X, and the inside X shoots.
coachingPoints: Inside player: get open, stick on the ice, and be ready for a quick shot or a tip.
Outside players: move the puck quickly and look for the inside pass first.
Drive the post and fight for net-front position.
Only one player per team in the circle at a time.
steps: Put two nets facing each other inside a faceoff circle, with a goalie in each.
Three per team: one inside the circle, two outside. Only one player per team may be inside.
The coach puts a puck in.
Outside players pass it around and try to get it to their inside player. They can shoot too.
Play short shifts and change on the coach's whistle. Optional, if time allows.

drills.title: Half-ice 3v3
drills.subtitle: O tries to score. D must win the puck AND pass it to the coach at the blue line. Then O flips to D, fresh 3 on O.
drills.blurb: 3 on 3 in half the ice. The O try to score. The D try to win the puck and pass it to the coach at the blue line. Then the D come off, the O flip to D, and three fresh skaters come on as O.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Half-ice 3v3. The O carry in and pass to a teammate in the slot, who shoots. A D player wins the rebound, passes to a teammate, who passes to the coach at the blue line. The D then go to the waiting line.
coachingPoints: O: support the puck carrier and get someone to the net.
D: win the puck, then move it quickly and with control to the coach.
Talk: who has the puck carrier, who has the net front.
Change fast so the next group can start right away.
steps: Use each half of the ice with a net in its normal spot. The coach stands at the blue line.
3 O try to score on 3 D.
The D must win the puck and pass it to the coach.
When the coach has the puck, the D come off, the O flip to D, and 3 fresh skaters come on as O.
Progression: all 3 D must touch the puck before passing to the coach.

drills.title: Defend the Cone
drills.subtitle: 1 on 1 at a faceoff circle: the attacker tries to touch the cone at the dot, the defender keeps body position.
drills.blurb: A backup when you run out of nets: defend a cone instead. 1 on 1 around a faceoff circle with a cone on the dot. The attacker tries to touch the cone with the puck; the defender stays between the attacker and the cone.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Defend the Cone. An attacker carries the puck around the faceoff circle while the defender mirrors from inside, then the attacker cuts in for the cone at the dot and the defender angles them away.
coachingPoints: Defender: stay between the attacker and the cone, stick on the puck.
Use your angle, not a reach. Keep your feet moving.
Attacker: protect the puck with your body and change speed to get inside.
Variations: with or without a puck, with or without sticks.
steps: Put a cone on the faceoff dot. One line of attackers and one line of defenders.
The attacker carries the puck around the circle. The defender mirrors from inside.
The attacker cuts in and tries to touch the cone with the puck. The defender angles them away.
Swap: the attacker joins the defender line and the defender joins the attack line.

drills.title: Corner Pass to Half-Ice 1-on-1
drills.subtitle: Lines in both corners and at the centre cone. Centre passes to a corner, then defends. 1-on-1 in your half of the zone.
drills.blurb: A half-ice 1-on-1 drill with three lines. Two lines stand against the boards in the corners, and one line stands in the middle of the ice at a cone level with the tops of the faceoff circles, with the pucks. The centre player passes to the front of a corner line, then steps in to defend. The corner player carries up the wall and attacks 1-on-1, staying in their half of the zone (split down the middle), and shoots. The next rep goes to the other corner.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Corner Pass to Half-Ice 1-on-1. One line of F's stands against the boards in each corner, and a line of D's with pucks stands in the middle of the ice at a cone level with the tops of the faceoff circles. The front D passes to the front F in the bottom corner, then steps across into that half of the ice. The F carries up the wall, curls in and attacks 1-on-1 while the D skates backwards to defend on the inside. The F shoots on the goalie. Then the F goes to the centre line and the D goes to that corner line. The next rep goes to the other corner.
coachingPoints: Passer: a hard, flat pass to the corner player's stick, then go defend right away.
Attacker: catch it, get your feet moving up the wall, then attack the net with speed.
Stay in your half of the zone. The middle of the ice is the boundary.
D: stay between the attacker and the net, stick on the ice, take away the middle.
Shoot to score, then follow it for the rebound.
steps: Three lines: one against the boards in each corner, and one in the middle of the ice at a cone level with the tops of the faceoff circles. Pucks with the centre line. A goalie in the net.
The front centre player passes to the front of one corner line.
The corner player carries up the wall. The passer steps across into that half to defend.
1-on-1: the attacker curls in and attacks the net, staying in their half of the zone. The D skates backwards and stays on the inside.
The attacker shoots.
Rotation: the attacker goes to the centre line, the D goes to the corner line they defended. The next centre player passes to the other corner.

drills.title: Mirror Angling 2v1
drills.subtitle: F loops the cones while the D mirrors around the dot, then a quick 2v1 rush. Both attackers drive the net.
drills.blurb: A half-ice station. The F carries a loop around the cones while the D mirrors around the cone at the faceoff dot, working on angling. Then a second F joins and it's a quick 2v1 on net. Both attackers drive the net; the puck carrier can pass, shoot or delay on the wall. Uses 2 D and 4-6 F.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Mirror Angling 2v1. An F line at the top of the circle and an X line at the dot. The F loops cone 1 and rounds cone 2 toward the boards while the X mirrors around the cone below the dot and angles the carrier toward the wall. A second F drives the net, the carrier passes to them, and they shoot on the goalie.
coachingPoints: D: mirror the carrier, keep your stick on the ice, and angle them to the boards.
Close the gap with your feet, not a reach. Take away the middle.
F: protect the puck through the cones and keep your feet moving.
2v1: both attackers drive the net. Carrier reads the D: pass, shoot or delay on the wall.
Quick reps: one rush, then the next group.
steps: Set three cones: one below the faceoff dot for the D, and two by the F line. F's line up at the top of the circle with pucks; D's line up at the dot.
The F carries a loop around the first cone while the D pivots around the cone by the dot, mirroring the F.
The F rounds the second cone and cuts toward the net along the wall. The D angles them toward the boards.
A second F drives the net. It's 2v1: the carrier can pass, shoot or delay on the wall.
Play it out, then everyone returns to their line and the next group goes.

drills.title: 1v1 Puck Race to 2v1
drills.subtitle: Two players race for the puck. The winner attacks with a low-to-high pass; the loser defends the 2v1.
drills.blurb: Two players start side by side and race for a puck rimmed into the corner. The winner retrieves it and starts the attack with a low-to-high pass to a high player; the loser becomes the D. Then it's a 2v1 on net.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of 1v1 Puck Race to 2v1. A coach behind the net rims a puck into the corner. Two players start side by side near the net and race for it. The winner carries up the wall and passes low-to-high to a player at the top of the circle by a cone, who carries to the slot and shoots while the winner drives the net. The loser defends.
coachingPoints: Race: first three strides hard, and win body position on the puck.
Winner: protect the puck on the wall, then look up for the low-to-high pass.
High player: be ready, stick on the ice, and attack the net after the catch.
Loser: recover fast and defend the 2v1. Take away the pass and let the goalie have the shooter.
Attackers: drive the net for rebounds.
steps: Two players start side by side near the net. A high player waits at the top of the circle by a cone. The coach has pucks behind the net.
The coach rims a puck into the corner and both players race for it.
The winner retrieves the puck and carries up the wall.
The winner passes low-to-high to the high player.
The high player attacks and shoots while the winner drives the net. The loser defends the 2v1. Play it out, then the next pair goes.

drills.title: Rebounds: In-tight Hands
drills.subtitle: Small nets with a cone on each side. Bank the puck off the net, gather it in tight and shoot.
drills.blurb: A net-front station with small nets. Two cones sit on either side of the net. Facing the net, the player banks the puck off the net, gathers it in tight and shoots. A coach or the next player in line can bank it instead. 2-3 players per net.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Rebounds: In-tight Hands. Small nets sit at the bottom of the faceoff circles with a cone on each side. The front of the line passes the puck off the post, skates in to gather it beside the net, and shoots into the small net, then returns to the back of the line.
coachingPoints: Soft hands: cushion the puck as it comes off the net.
Quick release in tight. Don't wind up.
Stay low with your stick on the ice, ready for the bounce.
Shoot to score: look for the open side, high or low.
Keep it moving: 2-3 players per net, lots of reps.
steps: Set up small nets with a cone on each side. 2-3 players per net, pucks at the line.
Facing the net, the front of the line banks the puck off the net (or a coach/partner banks it).
Gather the rebound in tight beside the net.
Shoot quickly into the small net.
Back of the line. The next player goes.

drills.title: Goalie Rebound Game
drills.subtitle: The coach shoots on one goalie. That goalie tries to steer the rebound into the other goalie's net.
drills.blurb: A goalie game for rebound control. Two nets sit side by side, each with a goalie. The coach shoots on one goalie, who tries to deflect the rebound into the other goalie's net. Switch nets after 5-10 shots and keep score.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Goalie Rebound Game. Two nets sit side by side along the top of the zone, each with a goalie. The coach shoots from the circle at the right net, and that goalie steers the rebound toward the left net.
coachingPoints: Goalies: square up to the shooter and track the puck all the way in.
Control the rebound with your pads and stick. Steer it, don't just block it.
Recover fast: the other goalie can fire one back.
Coach: vary the shots (low to the pads, glove side, blocker side).
steps: Put two nets side by side, each with a goalie. The coach has pucks out front.
The coach shoots on one goalie.
That goalie tries to direct the rebound into the other goalie's net.
Alternate which goalie gets the shot.
Scoring: each goalie starts on 10. Lose 1 for a direct goal against you and 2 for a rebound steered into your net. First to 0 loses. Switch nets after 5-10 shots.

drills.title: Rondo Passing Progressions
drills.subtitle: Groups of 5-7 in a small circle: passers keep the puck away from a defender in the middle. Steal it and you swap.
drills.blurb: A small-area passing game. 4-5 passers around a 20x20 ft circle (a faceoff circle works) keep the puck away from 1-2 defenders in the middle. A defender who intercepts swaps with the passer. Rotate defenders every 30-60 seconds; points for 5+ passes in a row. Build it up through the progressions.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Rondo Passing. Five passers stand around a faceoff circle with one X defender in the middle. The puck goes from passer to passer across and around the circle, and the X intercepts the fourth pass. The X then takes that passer's spot and the passer moves to the middle.
coachingPoints: Head up: know where your next pass is going before the puck arrives.
Quick, flat passes. Move the puck before the defender closes.
Show a target with your stick and give the passer an option.
Defender: take away the middle pass with your stick and body.
Count passes out loud: 5+ in a row scores a point.
steps: Groups of 5-7. 4-5 passers around a small circle (20x20 ft, or a faceoff circle) and 1-2 defenders in the middle.
Progression 1: pass around the circle with no defender.
Progression 2: one puck, follow your pass. Then two pucks, follow your pass.
Progression 3: one puck and one defender. If the defender intercepts, they swap with the passer.
Progression 4: two defenders, one puck. Rotate defenders every 30-60 seconds; 5+ passes in a row scores a point.

drills.title: Zone Entries: Delay
drills.subtitle: Carry in wide, delay on the wall, then attack (top) or hit a catcher streaking to the slot (bottom).
drills.blurb: Two delay variations of the zone entry. Delay: carry in wide, stop and curl back up the wall to buy time, then attack the net. Delay, low-to-slot (dynamic): carry in and delay, then hit a catcher streaking to the net for a catch-and-shoot from the slot. The other two variations in this progression match Low-to-High: Give-and-Go and Low-to-High: D-to-D. Can also be run in the neutral zone or on small ice.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Zone Entries: Delay. Top: a forward carries wide over the blue line, curls back up the wall to delay, then cuts to the slot and shoots. Bottom: a forward carries wide and curls to delay while a catcher skates in from the neutral zone and streaks to the net; the carrier passes to the catcher, who shoots from the slot.
coachingPoints: Carry in wide with speed to push the D back.
Delay: stop and curl hard with the puck on your forehand, protecting it from the D.
Head up during the curl: look for the attack lane or the late player.
Catcher: time your streak so you hit the slot with speed, stick on the ice.
Pass to the stick in the slot; catch and shoot quickly.
steps: Lines of forwards with pucks at the boards in the neutral zone. For the low-to-slot variation, a catcher line waits in the middle.
Delay (top): carry in wide over the blue line.
Stop and curl back up the wall to delay.
Attack: cut to the slot and shoot.
Delay, low-to-slot (bottom): carry in wide and delay the same way. The catcher streaks to the net; the carrier passes to the slot and the catcher shoots.
The other two variations in this progression (delay, low-to-high to the slot; delay, low-to-high to the D) match Low-to-High: Give-and-Go and Low-to-High: D-to-D.

drills.title: Give-and-Go to Shot
drills.subtitle: Skate up the wall, give-and-go with the coach, round the pylon, take the return pass and drive in for a shot.
drills.blurb: A half-ice skate, pass and shoot combo built around the give-and-go, the first passing play U11s use in games. The player skates up the wall from the corner, takes a pass from the coach and gives it right back, rounds a pylon near the red line, takes a second pass from the coach and drives in for a shot. Adapted from Hockey Canada's U11 (Atom) skate/shoot combo.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Give-and-Go to Shot. A line of players starts in the bottom corner. The front player skates up the bottom wall; a coach in the middle of the zone passes to them and they pass it straight back. They keep skating, round a pylon near the red line, take a second pass from the coach and carry in to shoot on the goalie, then return to the back of the line.
coachingPoints: Give a target: stick on the ice, blade facing the coach.
Make eye contact with the passer before the puck comes.
One-touch pass back: cushion it and give it right back.
Keep your feet moving through the pylon; don't glide.
Drive the net after the catch and shoot to score.
steps: One line in the corner. A coach with pucks stands in the middle of the zone. A pylon near the red line on the same side.
The front player skates up the wall. The coach passes to them.
Give it right back to the coach (give-and-go) and keep skating toward the pylon.
Round the pylon. The coach passes again as you come out of the turn.
Drive in and shoot, then join the back of the line. Alternate sides each round.

drills.title: Stationary Partner Passing
drills.subtitle: Partners 10-13 ft apart pass back and forth: forehand, then backhand, then switch sides. Step back as passes get crisp.
drills.blurb: The U11 starting point for passing. Everyone pairs up with one puck, standing 10-13 ft (3-4 m) apart. Pass forehand back and forth, then backhand, then switch sides so the other player works the backhand. Step further apart as the passes get crisp. Good as a quick station or warm-up; works anywhere on the ice.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Stationary Partner Passing. Two pairs of players stand facing each other about 12 feet apart, one pair near each faceoff circle. In each pair the first player passes to the partner and the partner passes it back.
coachingPoints: Give a target: blade square to your partner, stick on the ice.
Sweep the puck, don't slap it. Follow through to your target.
Cushion the pass as it arrives: soft hands, let the blade give.
Eyes up: look at your partner before you pass.
Backhand too: cup the puck and follow through low.
steps: Everyone pairs up with one puck, partners facing each other 10-13 ft (3-4 m) apart.
Pass forehand to your partner.
Your partner cushions it and passes it back.
After 10 good passes, switch to backhand passes, then swap sides so you both work forehand and backhand.
When the passes are crisp, both take a step back and keep going.

drills.title: Breakout: D to the Wall
drills.subtitle: F passes to the D and gets open on the wall. D skates it behind the net, hits the F, then steps up and defends 1-on-1.
drills.blurb: The core breakout pattern with two players (Weiss Tech phase 1). The forward passes to the D on the dot, then loops low and opens up on the half-wall. The D skates the puck behind the net and passes to the forward on the wall, who carries up the boards and curls at a cone near the red line. The D doesn't stand still: after the pass the D steps up, then skates backwards and defends the forward 1-on-1 back into the zone.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Breakout: D to the Wall. Forwards line up at the top of the blue line; defence line up at the bottom faceoff dot. The forward passes to the D, then skates down through the slot and loops up to the top half-wall. The D carries behind the net to the top corner and passes to the forward on the wall. The forward carries up the wall and curls at a cone near the red line while the D steps up toward the blue line. Then the forward attacks wide and shoots, and the D skates backwards (dotted arrow) between the forward and the net.
coachingPoints: F: pivot to face the puck and keep your eyes on the D while you get open.
F: stop on the wall with your stick on the ice. Give a target.
D: look over your shoulder before you go behind the net, and move the puck quickly.
D: after the pass, step up fast, then pivot and skate backwards. Stay between the F and the net.
Catch it and go: feet moving up the wall right away, then attack with speed.
steps: Forwards line up on the blue line with pucks. The D going steps out to the faceoff dot; the other D wait behind.
The F passes to the D on the dot.
The D skates the puck behind the net. At the same time the F loops low and opens up on the half-wall.
The D passes to the F on the wall.
The F carries up the wall and curls at the cone near the red line. The D steps up toward the blue line.
1-on-1: the F attacks the net and shoots. The D skates backwards and stays between the F and the net. Both go to the back of their lines.
Variation: see D-to-Wall Breakout to 2-on-1. A centre swings with the winger and they attack 2-on-1 against the D.

drills.title: D-to-Wall Breakout to 2-on-1
drills.subtitle: Same breakout: D skates it behind the net and hits the winger on the wall. The centre swings with him. 2-on-1 back in against the D.
drills.blurb: The 2-on-1 version of Breakout: D to the Wall. Same start: the winger passes to the D on the dot and gets open on the half-wall, and the D skates it behind the net and hits the winger. Then the winger carries up the wall while a centre from the second line swings out with him. Both curl at a cone near the red line and attack 2-on-1 against the D who made the pass. The D steps up, then skates backwards and takes away the pass.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of D-to-Wall Breakout to 2-on-1. Wingers line up at the top of the blue line with pucks, centres at the bottom of the blue line, and defence at the bottom faceoff dot. The winger passes to the D, loops low and opens up on the top half-wall. The D carries behind the net and passes to the winger on the wall. The winger carries up the wall and curls at a cone near the red line; the centre skates out and curls at a second cone; the D steps up. On the 2-on-1 the winger carries in and passes across to the centre while the D skates backwards (dotted arrow) through the middle, and the centre shoots.
coachingPoints: Same start: winger opens up on the wall with the stick on the ice; D moves the puck quickly.
Centre: time your swing so you curl at the cone with the winger and come in with speed.
Attackers: stay wide apart. The puck carrier drives the net; pass only if the D takes you.
D: step up, then skate backwards through the middle. Take away the pass and let the shooter come wide.
Shooter: stick on the ice, ready for the pass, shoot quickly.
steps: Wingers line up at the top of the blue line with pucks, centres at the bottom of the blue line. The D going steps out to the faceoff dot; the other D wait behind.
The winger passes to the D on the dot.
The D skates the puck behind the net. At the same time the winger loops low and opens up on the half-wall.
The D passes to the winger on the wall.
The winger carries up the wall while the centre swings out. Both curl at their cone near the red line. The D steps up.
2-on-1: the winger carries in and passes across to the centre. The D skates backwards through the middle and tries to stop the pass.
The centre shoots. Everyone goes to the back of their own line.
Variation: see Breakout: D to the Wall for the 1-on-1 version.

drills.title: Controlled-Skating Breakout
drills.subtitle: D skates the puck behind the net while the F glides through 4 spots, showing a target at each. D passes on time; F attacks 1-on-0.
drills.blurb: A timing and support drill for young players (Weiss Tech). The forward passes to the D, then skates slowly through four receiving spots marked with cones (high slot, low corner, half-wall, high on the wall), showing a target at each one. The D skates the puck behind the net and passes when the forward arrives at a spot, then the forward attacks 1-on-0. This half-ice version curls at a cone near the red line and attacks the same net.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Controlled-Skating Breakout. A forward line waits at the blue line and a D line at the bottom faceoff dot. Four numbered cones mark receiving spots on the top side: high slot, low by the boards, half-wall, and high on the wall. The F passes to the D, who carries behind the net. The F glides from spot 1 to spot 4; the D passes at spot 4. The F carries out, curls at a cone near the red line and shoots on the goalie.
coachingPoints: Control skate: slow and smooth, arriving at each spot on time.
Show a target at every spot: stick on the ice, blade facing the puck.
Never take your eyes off the puck.
D: pass when the F is ready, not before. Hard and flat to the forehand.
After the catch, attack with speed and shoot to score.
steps: Forwards line up at the blue line, D at the faceoff dot. Place four cones as receiving spots: high slot, low by the boards, half-wall, and high on the wall.
The F passes to the D, who pivots toward the boards and skates the puck behind the net.
The F skates slowly through spots 1, 2 and 3, showing a target at each.
The F arrives at spot 4 and the D passes on time.
The F carries out, curls at the cone near the red line and attacks 1-on-0.
Option: the coach calls which spot gets the pass. Later, add a D at the far blue line for a 1-on-1.

drills.title: Wide Entry, Drive the Net
drills.subtitle: Carry in wide over the blue line, keep your feet moving around the cone, cut to the net and shoot.
drills.blurb: The simplest U11 zone entry: wide with speed, then drive the net. The player carries the puck wide over the blue line, keeps their feet moving around a cone inside the zone, cuts to the net and shoots, then follows the shot for the rebound. Progression: add a D at the blue line for a 1-on-1. From a Hockey Canada U11 zone-entry station.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Wide Entry, Drive the Net. A line of forwards waits at the red line by the bottom boards with pucks. The front player carries wide along the boards over the blue line, turns tightly around a cone near the bottom of the circle, cuts toward the net and shoots on the goalie, then skates in for the rebound.
coachingPoints: Go wide with speed to push the defender back.
Keep your feet moving around the cone. No gliding.
Protect the puck on the turn: body between the cone and the puck.
Cut hard to the net and shoot in stride.
Follow your shot for the rebound.
steps: One line at the red line by the boards, with pucks. A cone inside the blue line, wide near the bottom of the circle. A goalie in net.
Carry the puck wide over the blue line with speed.
Go around the cone with your feet moving, then cut to the net.
Shoot, then drive the net for a rebound. Join the back of the line.
Alternate sides each round. Progression: add a D at the blue line for a 1-on-1.

drills.title: Three-Lane Wave Shooting
drills.subtitle: Three lanes go one after another: carry in, shoot, then clear out to the side so the next shooter has room.
drills.blurb: Lots of shots and simple to run. Three lines wait at the red line (left, middle, right lanes), each with pucks. One player from each lane carries in and shoots, one after another, and clears out to the side so the next shooter has a clear lane. The goalie gets a short reset between waves. From a Hockey Canada U9 practice plan.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Three-Lane Wave Shooting. Three lines labelled 1, 2 and 3 wait at the red line in the top, middle and bottom lanes, each with pucks. Lane 1 carries in and shoots from the top slot, lane 2 from the middle, and lane 3 from the bottom slot, one after another. Each shooter clears out along the side and returns to their own line.
coachingPoints: Head up while you carry; pick your spot before you shoot.
Shoot in stride, quick release.
Go when the player before you reaches the blue line.
After the shot, clear out to the side. Don't skate through the next shooter's lane.
Shoot to score: low blocker or low glove.
steps: Three lines at the red line (top, middle and bottom lanes), each with pucks. A goalie in net.
Lane 1 carries in and shoots.
Lane 2 goes when lane 1 reaches the blue line, and shoots. Lane 1 clears out to the side.
Lane 3 goes next and shoots. Lane 2 clears out.
Everyone returns to their own lane's line. The next wave goes when the goalie is set.

drills.title: 2-on-0 Wide and Middle
drills.subtitle: One goes wide with the puck, one drives the middle to the back post. Shoot (or pass), and both go to the net.
drills.blurb: Teaches one rule kids can remember: one goes wide, one drives the net. The puck carrier enters wide while the partner drives the middle lane to the back post. The carrier cuts in and shoots (or passes across to the back post), and both attackers go to the net for the rebound. Then switch lanes.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of 2-on-0 Wide and Middle. A wide line with pucks waits at the red line by the bottom boards and a middle line waits in the centre lane. The wide player carries over the blue line along the boards and cuts in toward the slot; the middle player skates straight down the middle and on to the back post. The wide player shoots and skates to the net front.
coachingPoints: Carrier: wide with speed, then cut in with your head up.
Middle player: drive hard to the back post, stick on the ice.
Shoot for a rebound, or pass across if the back post is open.
Both players go to the net after the shot.
Switch lanes every rep so everyone plays both roles.
steps: A wide line at the red line by the boards with pucks, and a middle line in the centre lane. A goalie in net.
The wide player carries over the blue line along the boards while the partner drives the middle lane.
The carrier cuts in; the middle player keeps going to the back post.
The carrier shoots (or passes across to the back post). Both go to the net for the rebound.
Switch lines: the carrier joins the middle line and the middle player joins the wide line.

drills.title: Figure-8s with Pivots
drills.subtitle: Skate a figure-8 around the two circles: forwards around the top circle, pivot to backwards at the cone on the bottom circle, pivot back to forwards at the next cone.
drills.blurb: A simple pivot drill. Players skate a figure-8 around the two end-zone circles: the top circle skating forwards, then on the bottom circle pivot from forwards to backwards at the first cone and back to forwards at the second. Pivots are the U10-U11 skill coaches most often skip, and they're needed for defence and for opening up to receive a pass. Add a puck once players are comfortable.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Figure-8s with Pivots. A line of skaters waits between the two faceoff circles near the blue line. The front skater skates forwards clockwise around the top circle, crosses diagonally to the bottom circle, pivots to backwards at cone 1, skates backwards around the bottom of the circle, pivots back to forwards at cone 2, and crosses back to the line.
coachingPoints: Pivot on the balls of your feet with knees bent. Stay low.
Keep your head and chest facing the same way through the pivot.
Don't stop: keep moving through every pivot.
Crossovers on the forward circle, C-cuts going backwards.
Pivot both ways: switch the direction of the figure-8 every few reps.
steps: One line between the two faceoff circles. Cones at two points on the bottom circle.
Skate forwards around the top circle.
Cross to the bottom circle and pivot to backwards at cone 1.
Skate backwards to cone 2, pivot back to forwards and finish the figure-8.
Back of the line. The next skater goes when you reach cone 1. Later, do it with a puck.

drills.title: Full-Ice Figure-8 Shooting
drills.subtitle: Up the wall, swing through centre, curl around the far circle, cut to the net and shoot. Both corners go.
drills.blurb: A full-ice skating drill with a puck and a shot. Each player carries up the wall, swings through centre ice, curls around the far circle and cuts to the net to shoot. Lines in opposite corners go at the same time, so the two paths make a figure-8 through the middle.
drills.diagramAlt: Full-ice diagram of Full-Ice Figure-8 Shooting. Lines with pucks sit in the bottom-left and top-right corners. Each player carries up the wall to the blue line, swings up through centre ice and back down to the far blue line, curls around the outside of the far faceoff circle, cuts to the net and shoots. The two paths cross at centre ice like a figure-8.
coachingPoints: Keep your feet moving the whole way. Crossovers on the curves.
Head up crossing centre ice: the other line is coming the other way.
Curl tight around the outside of the circle with the puck on your forehand.
Cut to the net with speed and shoot to score. Follow it for a rebound.
Start without pucks if the group is new to it.
steps: Setup: a line with pucks in two opposite corners and a goalie in each net.
Carry the puck up the wall to the blue line.
Swing up through centre ice and back down to the far blue line.
Curl around the outside of the far faceoff circle.
Cut to the net and shoot.
Join the line in the corner at that end. Both corners go at the same time; the next player goes when the one ahead reaches centre.

drills.title: Two-Line 2-on-0 Flow
drills.subtitle: Partners pass back and forth all the way up the ice, then attack 2-on-0 and shoot. Both ends go.
drills.blurb: Partners pass back and forth in two lanes the whole length of the ice, then attack 2-on-0: the winger passes to the centre in the middle for the shot and drives the net. A pair from the other end goes at the same time on the other half of the ice, so everyone stays busy.
drills.diagramAlt: Full-ice diagram of Two-Line 2-on-0 Flow. At each end a centre line and a winger line wait below the goal line on one side. The pair skates up the ice in two lanes, passing back and forth three times. In the far zone the winger passes to the centre in the middle, the centre shoots and the winger drives the net. The pair from the other end does the same on the other half of the ice.
coachingPoints: Pass hard and flat, a stick-length ahead of your partner.
Give a target: stick on the ice, blade facing the passer.
Stay in your lane and keep your speed. Don't drift toward your partner.
Finish: the shooter shoots to score, the other player drives the net for a rebound.
steps: Setup: at each end, a centre line and a winger line wait below the goal line on the same side, with pucks at the centre line. A goalie in each net.
The centre passes to the winger and both skate up the ice in their lanes.
The winger passes back to the centre.
The centre passes to the winger again across the far blue line.
The winger passes to the centre in the middle. The centre shoots and the winger drives the net.
Both join the lines at that end. The pair from the other end goes at the same time on the other half of the ice.

drills.title: Breakout to 1-on-1
drills.subtitle: D skates it out and hits the F on the wall, then pivots and skates backward. 1-on-1 the length of the ice.
drills.blurb: A breakout pass that turns into a full-length 1-on-1. The D skates the puck out of the corner and passes to the forward on the wall, then pivots and skates backward. The forward carries up the ice and tries to beat the D for a shot on the far goalie.
drills.diagramAlt: Full-ice diagram of Breakout to 1-on-1. A D line waits in the top-left corner with pucks and a forward line in the bottom-left corner. The D carries the puck out to the middle while the forward skates to the half-wall. The D passes to the forward, then pivots and skates backward up the middle. The forward carries up the wall and through the neutral zone, and the D stays between the forward and the net to the far end, where the forward shoots on the goalie.
coachingPoints: F: back to the boards on the wall, stick on the ice, catch it and go.
D: hard, flat pass to the forehand, then a quick pivot to backward.
D: keep your gap. Stay between the F and the net, stick on the ice.
F: use your speed, attack the D's outside, and shoot to score.
Both: go back to your lines after the shot, then switch D and F.
steps: Setup: a D line with pucks in one corner and a forward line in the other corner of the same end. A goalie in each net.
The D skates the puck out of the corner while the F skates to the half-wall.
The D passes to the F on the wall, then pivots to skate backward.
The F carries up the wall while the D backs up through the middle.
1-on-1 through the neutral zone: the D keeps a good gap.
The F tries to beat the D and shoots on the far goalie. Both go back to their lines.

drills.title: Stickhandling Obstacle Course
drills.subtitle: Weave the cones, pull the puck through the gate, puck under the stick, then shoot.
drills.blurb: A puck-control course in one zone. Skaters weave a line of cones, pull the puck through a two-cone gate, slide the puck under a raised stick and step over it, then curl into the slot and shoot. The next skater goes when the one ahead reaches the gate.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of the Stickhandling Obstacle Course. One line with pucks stands at the blue line near the bottom boards. The skater weaves through four cones along the bottom, turns up through a two-cone gate near the goal line, carries left between two cones where a stick is laid across, then curls into the slot and shoots on the goalie.
coachingPoints: Soft hands: cup the puck, don't slap at it.
Eyes up between the cones. Feel the puck, don't stare at it.
Gate: pull the puck across your body, then push it through.
Stick: slide the puck under, step over, pick it up on the other side.
Finish strong: shoot in stride to score.
steps: One line at the blue line with pucks. Set up 4 cones in a line, a 2-cone gate, and a stick resting across two cones.
Weave through the cones with the puck.
Pull the puck through the gate.
Slide the puck under the stick and step over it.
Curl into the slot and shoot. Go to the back of the line.
The next skater goes when the one ahead reaches the gate.

drills.title: Tight Turns Around the Dots
drills.subtitle: Skate the length of the ice and tight-turn all the way around 5 faceoff dots. No pucks first, then with pucks.
drills.blurb: A full-ice edge drill. Skaters start in the corner and skate the length of the ice, doing a full tight turn around five faceoff dots in a zig-zag: an end-zone dot, a neutral-zone dot, centre ice, the other neutral-zone dot, and the far end-zone dot. Run it without pucks first, then with pucks.
drills.diagramAlt: Full-ice diagram of Tight Turns Around the Dots. A line starts in the bottom-left corner. The skater does a full tight turn around a cone on the bottom-left end-zone dot, the top-left neutral-zone dot, the centre dot, the bottom-right neutral-zone dot and the top-right end-zone dot, then sprints to the far goal line.
coachingPoints: Knees bent, inside knee deep, lean into the turn.
Inside edge on the outside foot, outside edge on the inside foot.
Head and stick lead you around the dot.
Push out of the turn with crossovers.
With pucks: keep the puck on the inside of the turn, close to your feet.
steps: Put a cone on 5 faceoff dots. One line starts in the corner.
Skate to dot 1 and tight-turn all the way around it.
Skate to dot 2 and tight-turn.
Tight-turn at centre ice (dot 3), then dot 4.
Tight-turn at dot 5 and sprint to the far goal line. Come back down the boards.
The next skater goes when the one ahead reaches dot 2. Then do it again with pucks.

drills.title: Explosive Starts Race
drills.subtitle: Race a partner from the goal line to the blue line. V-start first, then crossover start.
drills.blurb: A quick race for first-step speed. Two lines stand on the goal line. A pair races to the blue line using a V-start, then glides back along the boards. Next round the pair uses a crossover start, standing sideways and crossing over on the first step.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of the Explosive Starts Race. Two lines stand on the goal line, one on each side of the net. The front player of each line sprints straight to the blue line. Then they glide back along the boards to the back of their line.
coachingPoints: V-start: heels together, toes out, short quick steps.
Stay low and drive your knees forward.
Crossover start: stand sideways, first step crosses over toward where you're going.
Arms pump forward and back, not side to side.
Race to the line, don't coast.
steps: Two lines on the goal line, one on each side of the net.
Round 1: V-start. The front pair races to the blue line.
Glide back along the boards to the back of your line.
Round 2: crossover start. Stand sideways and cross over on your first step.
Switch lines so you race from both sides.

drills.title: Backward C-Cuts
drills.subtitle: Waves skate backwards with C-cuts from the goal line to the far blue line. Variation: forwards to red, pivot, backwards.
drills.blurb: A full-ice backwards skating drill in waves. Four lanes start on the goal line and skate backwards with C-cuts to the far blue line, then glide back along the boards. Variation: skate forwards to the red line, pivot, then skate backwards to the far blue line.
drills.diagramAlt: Full-ice diagram of Backward C-Cuts. Four lanes of skaters start on the left goal line. Each skates backwards (dotted arrows) in a straight lane to the far blue line.
coachingPoints: Sit low like you're in a chair. Chest up, eyes up.
Push out in a C shape and pull your skate back under you.
Switch feet each push. Keep your shoulders square.
Stick on the ice in front of you.
Pivot: turn your hips, not just your shoulders, and keep your feet moving.
steps: 4 lanes on the goal line.
Skate backwards with C-cuts to the far blue line.
Glide back along the boards.
Variation: forwards to the red line, pivot, then backwards to the far blue line.

drills.title: Triangle Passing on the Move
drills.subtitle: Groups of 3 skate up the ice in a triangle: middle to wing, across to the far wing, back to the middle, shoot.
drills.blurb: A three-player passing rush. Three lines start at centre ice. The middle player passes to a wing, the wing passes across to the far wing, and the far wing passes back to the middle player driving the net, who shoots. Everyone switches lines.
drills.diagramAlt: Half-ice diagram of Triangle Passing on the Move. Three lines start at centre ice: one middle, one on each wing. All three skate into the zone. The middle player passes to the bottom wing, the bottom wing passes across to the top wing, and the top wing passes to the middle player driving the net, who shoots on the goalie.
coachingPoints: Keep the triangle: wings wide, middle trailing a little.
Pass ahead of your teammate's stick so they don't slow down.
Stick on the ice, ready for the pass.
Middle player: drive the net hard after your pass.
Call for the puck.
steps: Three lines at centre ice: middle (with pucks), left wing, right wing.
All three go. The middle passes to a wing.
That wing passes across to the far wing.
The far wing passes to the middle player driving the net.
The middle player shoots.
Switch lines and skate back to centre.

drills.title: Backhand Shooting
drills.subtitle: Backhands only: one from the slot, then drive the net and backhand it to the far post.
drills.blurb: A backhand-only shooting drill. One line comes into the slot and takes a backhand shot. The other line drives the net from the wing and puts a backhand on the far post. Switch lines after each shot.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Backhand Shooting. Two lines at the blue line with pucks. The top line carries into the slot and shoots a backhand. The bottom line carries wide along the boards, cuts to the net and shoots a backhand to the far post.
coachingPoints: Puck on the backhand side, near your back foot.
Sweep it forward and roll your wrists to lift it.
Follow through high toward the target.
Driving the net: protect the puck with your body, aim far post.
Follow your shot for the rebound.
steps: Two lines at the blue line with pucks.
Slot line: carry into the slot and shoot a backhand.
Wing line: drive the net from the wing and backhand it to the far post.
Switch lines after each shot so you drive from both sides.

drills.title: Puck Protection in the Circle
drills.subtitle: 1-on-1 inside a faceoff circle. Protect the puck for 10 seconds with your body. The D tries to knock it out.
drills.blurb: A 1-on-1 puck protection battle in both end-zone circles. The puck carrier must stay inside the circle and keep the puck for 10 seconds, using their body and edges. The defender tries to knock the puck out of the circle. Then switch roles and the next pair goes.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Puck Protection in the Circle. A puck carrier and a defender are in each end-zone faceoff circle, with lines waiting at the blue line. The carrier skates around the inside of the circle with the puck, turning their back to the defender, while the defender chases.
coachingPoints: Body between the D and the puck.
Puck on the far side, away from the D's stick.
Knees bent, wide stance, keep your feet moving.
Use tight turns to spin away.
D: stick on the puck, stay on the inside.
steps: A pair in each faceoff circle: a puck carrier and a defender. Lines wait at the blue line.
Whistle: protect the puck inside the circle.
Turn your back to the D and keep the puck away.
After 10 seconds, switch roles. Then the next pair goes.

drills.title: Sharks and Minnows
drills.subtitle: Minnows with pucks try to cross the zone. Sharks knock pucks away. Lose your puck and you become a shark.
drills.blurb: A fun stickhandling game. Minnows with pucks start on the blue line and try to cross the zone to the goal line. Sharks in the middle knock pucks away. Lose your puck and you become a shark. Go back and forth until one minnow is left.
drills.diagramAlt: Zone diagram of Sharks and Minnows. Four minnows with pucks start on the blue line. Two sharks wait in the middle. The minnows carry across toward the goal line. One shark knocks a minnow's puck away, and that minnow skates into the middle to become a shark.
coachingPoints: Head up: see the sharks before they reach you.
Protect the puck: body between the shark and the puck.
Change speed and direction to get past.
Sharks: stick on the ice, take away space.
Keep it fair: stick on puck, no slashing.
steps: Minnows with pucks line up on the blue line. Start with 2 sharks in the middle.
Go! Minnows try to cross to the goal line.
Sharks knock pucks away. If you lose your puck, you become a shark.
Cross back. Keep going until one minnow is left.
